Both match blocks fall THROUGH to the shipped value, so an unrecognised string is the shipped behaviour too. THREE appearances, none of which reaches an axis key: PhysicsSim_Springs places cloth_simulation:0:1 (token:rotation:y_offset - neither is config), PhysicsSimulation_Cloth_Simulation places the bare token, and Curation_Bay_physicssimulation_2 carries it inside a curation_station roster (curation_station#artifacts:soft_bodies,cloth_simulation). The grid calls apply_grid_config DEFERRED, and curation_station calls it with {emissive: false} AFTER add_child; in both cases _ready has already run, no axis key is present, the build signature is unchanged, and the function returns before touching a node. ArtifactIdentity.stamp, which runs BEFORE add_child, reads default_params and nothing else - this entry has none - so neither the axes nor the fixture can reach a map placement.
dna.was: two hard-coded literals inside _apply_constraints - 'for iter in 3' and '* 0.5' - and a rest length that was never a decision. THE STIFFNESS SLIDER IS NOT CONNECTED TO ANYTHING: cloth_stiffness (100.0) and cloth_damping (5.0) are read exactly twice in the file, both times in _setup_controls to seed a slider's default position. No force reads either one. So the @identity's declared critical_parameter - 'k (stiffness) - low k = jelly cloth, high k = rigid sheet' - is wired to nothing, and a player in VR can move the STIFFNESS slider all afternoon while no force in the simulation reads it. The knob actually doing that job shipped unnamed, inside the solver loop. And _add_spring set every rest length to the distance the particles were BUILT at, which says the cloth has exactly as much material as the space it occupies - a claim about garment cutting that nobody made on purpose.
dna.note: An under-relaxed position solver does not converge more slowly to the same drape - IT HAS A DIFFERENT FIXED POINT, and that is what makes this axis a still rather than a rate. Each step injects gravity as a position increment and each pass corrects only a fraction of the resulting overstretch, so equilibrium sits where injection equals correction and the residual stretch scales as roughly 1 / (iterations x gain): nudged 2.86, worked 0.67, pressed 0.21, held 0.10 in the same units. nudged hangs visibly longer, its springs permanently stretched, sagging into a deep catenary between its two pins and pooling on the floor; held is near-rigid, its spring lines drawn as a regular lattice with almost no stretch. All four are AT REST and they are different lengths. ease is the orthogonal half: relaxation is how hard the springs insist on a rest length, ease is what that rest length IS, and its four values differ in total surface AREA, which no settle time can change - taut contracts to 82% and pulls into a stretched membrane with straight edges, full carries 40% surplus (96% more area) into deep drapery folds that puddle around the sphere's base instead of stretching over it. Ordinal order is nudged < worked < pressed < held and taut < plain < slack < full; the registry lists the export default leftmost because apply_dna_block.py puts it there.
dna.shared_with: verlet_workbench.relaxation - same word, same four values, same claim, TWO DIFFERENT SOLVERS, declared in the same wave. That is the house pattern (cloth_straps took spring_system.suspension character for character; nine benches share assay), and it buys a cross-check the corpus does not otherwise have: a shared vocabulary that is honest measures ALIKE. If these two come back with wildly different magnitudes, the first suspect is one of the two HARNESSES, not one of the two designs.
dna.declined: wind_strength (3.0) and gravity_strength (9.8), plus cloth_damping and the hard-coded 0.995 velocity decay. wind_strength is the @identity's own named source of 'drama' and it visibly transforms the cloth - and it is refused because the wind here is not a steady load but a DRIVE: wind_dir rotates forever as (sin(0.7t), 0, cos(0.5t)) and the per-node term is a sine of _time, so at any wind_strength above zero there is no rest shape to photograph, only an instant. Zeroing it is the fixture's first job. cloth_damping and the 0.995 decay are pure RATES: two values reach the same drape, one sooner. Declining them by name is the whole point of this wave - the sequence's subject is dynamics, so the axis has to change the shape the material comes to REST in, not how fast it gets there.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: relaxation: PRESSED vs HELD, the tight end of the ordinal ladder - 0.11 residual units apart against nudged-to-held's 2.76, a 25:1 ratio. Predict frame ~1.1% and focus ~5%, i.e. BELOW the 3% bite bar, which is expected on the tight end of an ordinal ladder rather than a fault; predict nudged vs held frame ~14%, focus ~45%. ease: PLAIN vs SLACK, 18% apart against taut-to-full's 71%. Arithmetic: the pinned cloth is 1.5 m wide at scale 0.8, and an 18% surplus deepens its sag by about 0.18 x 1.5 x 0.5 = 0.135 m; against a subject roughly 7.3 m wide across three cloths that is a ~1.8% linear change over ~35% of the frame's occupied area, so predict frame ~5% and focus ~18%, the hottest 5% landing on the hems where the whole change is.
dna.fixture_why: THE AXIS IS A RESTING SHAPE AND THIS ARTIFACT DOES NOT REST. Three separate things made two runs of the same value differ, each fatal to a verdict. (1) The wind is a drive, not a load - see declined - and zeroing wind_strength ALONE is not enough, because _apply_forces reads wind_dir * (wind_strength + wind_noise) and wind_noise was an inline * 0.5, so that would leave a +/-0.5 N oscillating force still driving the cloth: a fixture that looks like it worked and did not. wind_noise_amp is a NEW export holding that literal, default 0.5 (exactly representable, so the shipped path is the same product and not a value that rounds to it), and it has to be zeroed too. (2) '_time += delta' and 'node.update(delta)' integrated with the RENDER delta, so the state at capture depended on how many frames the machine happened to draw - frame-rate coupled, which is worse than merely unsettled. fixed_step (new, default 0.0 = use the render delta, the shipped path) pins the step. (3) Nothing had settled by the sweep's ~1.45 s anyway: the 0.995 per-step decay still holds 0.995^87 = 65% of any residual after 87 frames, and the pendulum period of a 1.5 m cloth is about 2.5 s. settle_steps (new, default 0 = off) runs that many fixed 1/60 sub-steps synchronously at the END of the build with _time HELD AT 0 - which makes the wind term a constant instead of a function of the clock, and exactly zero under this fixture - so the cloth is at its fixed point BEFORE the first frame is drawn and 1.45 s stops mattering. 420 steps is 7 s of simulated time; the 0.995 per-step decay leaves 0.995^420 = 12% of any residual velocity, and all three cloths sit on attractors (two pinned corners; the floor clamp at y=0 with velocity.y zeroed; a pinned top edge over a fixed sphere). The pre-pass renders once at the end so the sweep's AABB pre-pass measures the resting pose and not the build-time flat grid. There is NO RNG anywhere in this file - no randf, no randi, no RandomNumberGenerator - so law 4 has nothing to seed here; every source of run-to-run difference in this artifact was the clock. All three exports default to the shipped behaviour exactly, so nothing that ships today runs a single extra step. WHAT 'REST' ACTUALLY MEANS HERE, and it is not what it sounds like: the constraint solver is position-based and NEVER TOUCHES VELOCITY, and _apply_forces contributes only gravity once the wind is zeroed, so a free node's velocity is not bounded by the springs at all - it runs to a terminal 9.8 x (1/60) / 0.005 = 32.67 m/s downward. The resting shape is therefore a BALANCE between a fixed downward drift per step and the correction the relaxation passes can undo, which is exactly why iterations x gain sets the shape and not merely the speed - but it is a moving equilibrium, not a static one. The consequence for this fixture, stated so nobody has to rediscover it: 420 steps leaves the velocity at 28.54 of 32.67 m/s, i.e. 87% of terminal, so the pre-pass has NOT fully converged. Drift per step is 0.476 m at the end of the pre-pass and 0.499 m by the shutter at ~507 total steps. Determinism therefore rests on that drift being insensitive to the frame count rather than on true convergence: a +/-20 frame difference in how many _process calls precede the capture moves the drift about 1%, against axis separations of 25:1 between the extreme values, so the verdict is safe by two orders of magnitude but the frame is not bit-identical between runs on different machines. 1200 steps would put velocity at 99.3% of terminal and make it airtight; it is NOT used because at held (10 iterations) that is 1200 x 3 cloths x 290 springs x 10 = 10.4M spring corrections synchronously inside _ready, against 3.65M at 420, and the boot budget is a 45 s watchdog grace shared across eight variants. 420 is the compromise, chosen with the arithmetic in hand rather than by hope.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config compares _build_signature() - [cloth_resolution, relaxation, ease, settle_steps, fixed_step, wind_strength, wind_noise_amp, gravity_strength], every value the build reads - against the signature recorded at the END of _ready, and RETURNS BEFORE TOUCHING A NODE when they are equal. That early return is what keeps the existing placements bit-identical, because the grid calls apply_grid_config deferred and a call carrying the values the build already used is then a no-op. It also returns early when _is_built is false - a composer that configures BEFORE parenting, where _ready has not run and will build with the values just written. A real change calls _rebuild_sim, which frees only _sim_owned (the three cloths' MultiMeshInstance3D and ImmediateMesh renderers plus the two collision-sphere meshes) and rebuilds them; the labels, the RackTemplates control panel and the VR controller signal connections are built once in _ready and survive, so a rebuild cannot connect a controller twice. THIRTEEN appearances, each read out of its map JSON for this pass, and NOT ONE of them carries a `#key:value` tail: five grid tokens (SoftBodies_Obsticals as `flagdancer:90`, and SoftBodies_Obsticals_p1 / _p2 / _p3 / Corridor_SoftBodies_Obsticals as the bare word - a rotation suffix is not a config, so merged_config is empty and apply_grid_config is never called), seven `exhibit_furniture#kind:floor_work#size:l#mount:flagdancer` mounts (Trial_castelvecchio / grande / kanazawa / lattice_pm_17 / sainsbury / uffizi / wfc_softbodies), and the Curation_Bay_softbodies_0 curation_station roster. The maps have been describing something else for months: SoftBodies_Obsticals/critical.md says the flag is 'pinned at one edge - attached, constrained, unable to leave its pole', and technical.md says 'A cloth surface pinned along one edge'. No line of code ever pinned an edge. `heading=hoist` is the value that makes this artifact do what its own documentation has been claiming it does.
dna.note: `crimp` is NEW and free corpus-wide - the textile word for the wave standing in a fabric. Not `fold` (polyhedron_nets_cube: whether a net is folded, a discrete state); not `swell` (marching_cubes: terrain amplitude class); not `weave` (ruth_asawa_sculpture: which wire topology gets emitted, a construction, where crimp is a deformation of one fixed construction). `heading` is NEW - the vexillological and curtain-making name for the reinforced edge a cloth is attached by. Deliberately NOT `suspension` (cloth_straps, spring_system): that axis names the FURNITURE a hanging body hangs from and builds a rank of steel around an untouched cloth. This one builds nothing and moves no prop; it changes which part of the cloth is allowed to move. Not `anchorage` (ant_colony_v2, nest-site arrangement), not `hang` (gallery_winner_showcase, the arrangement of hung objects), not `attach` (point: float/stake/plate). Both axes were chosen for the only property of a wave that survives being frozen - its SHAPE ALONG THE CLOTH - because everything in this sequence moves and the evidence is one still.
dna.declined: `wind_strength` (1.0), the @identity's own declared critical_parameter and the most tempting knob in the file. Refused because at a frozen phase it is nothing but a uniform amplitude multiplier on a sine: four values are four SCALINGS of one shape, which the union-AABB camera then partly divides back out again, and in motion it reads as speed-of-flapping rather than as form. `celebration_intensity` is worse - it is consulted only while `celebration_mode` is true, and celebration_mode can only be turned on by a live ui_accept press that no capture will ever make, so all four values would render byte-identically. dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED THERE IS NO DETERMINISM HERE, TWICE OVER, and 'has it settled by 1.45 s' is not even the right question: there is no simulation to settle. The pose is a closed-form function of `t = Time.get_ticks_msec() * 0.001 + time_offset`, so the flag is never at rest and the shutter photographs the wall clock; and `time_offset = randf() * TAU` is drawn off the global generator with no seed, which is five different objects across five variants. (The file LOOKS like it seeds something - `var noise_seed := int(time_offset * 1000) % 1000` - and that local is never read again. Decoration, not a seed. The second random draw the brief warns about, `randf_range(0.8, 1.2)`, is inside create_flag_parade(), which nothing in the repository calls.) frozen_phase 2.35 makes t a constant, so time_offset is never read, the flag is MOTIONLESS, and the picture is a pure function of the exports on every machine. 2.35 rather than a round number because it gives a well-spread wave at the default - bone 0 at sin(4.70) = -1.000, bone 8 at sin(6.70) = +0.405, bone 16 at sin(8.70) = +0.666, all times 0.4 - where a near-flat instant would flatter every value equally. wave_seed 20260812 is for the WORLD, not the bench: in a live map the phase must keep running, and an explicit integer (never `rng.seed = randi()`, which is the opposite of seeding) makes it the same flag on every launch. Both are written as NUMBERS, not strings, because they are assigned straight onto typed float and int exports before _ready.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config checks each word against CRIMPS / HEADINGS, builds a signature of all four values, and RETURNS before assigning anything when it equals `_config_sig` - which _ready() primes with the shipped values, so a call carrying keys this artifact does not declare is a strict no-op. Nothing rebuilds geometry in any case: all four values are read fresh by _process every frame, so a live placement changes shape without a single node being freed. setup_joyful_animation() re-runs only when the seed itself moved, so a config repeating the shipped -1 never spends a second randf() and never re-rolls a running flag. _ready() builds synchronously and there is no call_deferred in the build path. Teardown now frees an `_owned` array (skeleton, mesh, particles) instead of the shipped `for child in get_children(): if not child.owner: child.queue_free()`, which took down every node any other system had parented to this artifact at runtime.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: PREDICTED BEFORE ANY CAPTURE, and it disagrees with the design on BOTH axes, which is the only kind of prediction worth writing. Method: the sheet carries no material (see `finding`), so its interior is uniform and only the SILHOUETTE can differ; project each of the 17 bone columns with the canonical rig (world +Z maps to (-0.581, -0.209) screen metres at yaw 0.62 / pitch -0.26), rasterise the union of the 16 quads between columns, and take the symmetric difference. crimp: the design named ripple vs corrugation. WRONG - that pair is FOURTH of six. The closest is flat vs corrugation at 0.69% of the full frame (6.8% of the subject crop, ~2.3% critic frame), because at 1.2 rad per bone corrugation's wave averages out over the silhouette and its end column lands near where flat's does; ripple vs corrugation is 1.41% (~4.6% critic frame), a factor of 2.0 wider. Structural note the design missed: bone 0 has wave_offset = 0 * gradient = 0 for EVERY value, so all four crimp tiles share their left edge exactly and the difference grows linearly toward bone 16. heading: the design named hoist vs fly as the closest and the likeliest to miss the bar. It is the WIDEST of the six - 0.90% of frame at the swept default crimp=swell (2.9% critic frame). The closest is hoist vs both at 0.42% (4.1% of crop, ~1.4% critic frame), because the `both` bunting envelope and the `hoist` ramp agree at the dead hoist end and differ only over the fly half. On FOCUS both axes should saturate near 33% rather than separate, since every differing pixel is a full-contrast sheet-versus-background flip and the differing area exceeds the hottest-5% window: on a silhouette-only subject FOCUS IS THE WRONG DISCRIMINATOR and `frame` is the informative number. ALL OF THIS IS CONDITIONAL - see `finding`. The design also assumed the flag fills ~60% of frame; it is 9.5% at framing 1.0, a factor of 6.3, which is why every predicted percentage here is smaller than the design's.
dna.finding: DO NOT SWEEP THIS TOKEN YET - IT PHOTOGRAPHS AS A WHITE QUAD, AND THE AXES ARE NOT THE REASON. The only capture that exists (user://multi_shots/flagdancer, 2026-04-20, four angles) shows a single small white quadrilateral and no flag from any angle, and no commit has touched this folder since, so it is current. That quad is the .tscn's own vestigial 1x1 QuadMesh; the procedural 6x4 m flag is in the AABB and not in the picture - the camera had pulled back to about 15 m of framed extent, which is the 7.2 m mesh diagonal times the capturer's pad, so the mesh resource exists and draws nothing. Godot resolves that path at assignment and, with no explicit Skin, caches an auto-skin built from the rest transforms of nothing; the 17 bones added afterwards never regenerate it, so the surface is skinned against an empty bind array. Two working procedural skinned meshes in this repository do the opposite in both respects - commons/artifacts/ik_arm_demo (explicit Skin, bind poses set from `skeleton.get_bone_rest(i).affine_inverse()`, `skeleton` assigned LAST) and commons/hazards/octapod_crawler/one_leg (explicit Skin, MeshInstance3D parented UNDER the Skeleton3D). A pride flag that renders white. NEITHER IS FIXED IN THIS PASS, deliberately: both change what all 13 shipped placements look like, both are unverifiable without a Godot run, and this pass was forbidden one. The axes, the defaults and the fixture are complete and correct behind them.
dna.measurement_risk: Even once it renders, the subject is only 9.5% of frame at framing 1.0 - the AABB is 6 x 4 x ~0, a wide flat sheet, and PAD 1.9 on the DIAGONAL wastes most of the frame. dna.default: anvil=none - _build_anvil() returns on its first line before a single Node is constructed, so the tree is byte-identical to what shipped: anchor, upper arm, joint1, lower arm, joint2, with the paddle MeshInstance3D and its CollisionShape3D under the lower arm, in that order. All SIX placements are the bare token pendulum_slap in ONE map, SoftBodies_Obsticals_Part1 (interactables rows 2, 6 and 10) - no rotation suffix, no y_offset, no #key:value on any of them - and this entry carries no default_params and no delegate, so merged_config is empty and GridInteractablesComponent never calls apply_grid_config at all. The determinism exports are no-ops at their defaults too: initial_impulse 50.0 is the literal from apply_initial_impulse() and the deferred kick is only scheduled when it is non-zero; settle_damp 0.0 and lean_force 0.0 each guard their whole branch; paddle_size 1.5 short-circuits _paddle_extent() to the exact shipped Vector3(1.5, 1.5, 0.5) with no arithmetic in the path.
dna.was: an arm hitting air. setup_scene() and setup_soft_body() were both commented out in _ready(), soft_body_pressure was read by nothing in the file, and the README's promise - 'impulsive force meeting compliance' - had no compliance anywhere in the scene. Six placements of a slap test with nothing to slap, in the sequence whose truth line is that form emerges from the material's own dynamics.
dna.note: the axis names what is standing in the arm's path, and the four values are four compliances under one load: none is the shipped void, slab a rigid StaticBody3D box (all the deflection in the ARM), cushion a SoftBody3D membrane stretched in a rigid frame over a backing plate half a paddle-width behind it (deflection SHARED), curtain a SoftBody3D sheet pinned along its top row to a rail (the arm barely deflects; the cloth has no resistance to give, only travel). NOT `assay` (jelly_cube, softmill, revolving_joy_ride, softbody_gallery_part2): that word is the apparatus arranged AROUND a specimen, and the anvil is half the physics. NOT `substance` (breathing_room): that is the material a body is made OF. NOT `support` (code_display) - nothing here stands on anything - and NOT `suspension` (cloth_straps, spring_system) - nothing here hangs. The name is free corpus-wide. WHERE the anvil stands is DERIVED, not typed: an anvil further out than the arm's own driven rest angle is never touched and four values then photograph one picture, so _anvil_lean() computes atan(lean_force / (10 kg * g)) and stands it at 0.6 of that - 8.9 degrees off plumb against a free rest of 14.9 at the fixture. The soft surfaces are generated by _sheet_mesh() rather than taken from PlaneMesh, because SoftBody3D point indices are the solver's WELDED vertex order (an engine internal): a grid with no duplicate vertices makes vertex(row, col) == row * (cols + 1) + col a fact about the file, so set_point_pinned() needs no printed read-back to aim.
dna.declined: slap_force (20.0) and initial_impulse (50.0) - how hard the arm is kicked. The pendulum is a DOUBLE pendulum with PinJoint3Ds, zero damping and a kick delivered through call_deferred, so (a) it never comes to rest, (b) the number of physics ticks between the kick and the shutter is a fact about the machine, and (c) a driven double pendulum is chaotic - two runs at the same impulse are not two photographs of the same thing. Sweeping it would produce confidently different tiles and a bite number that is pure frame clock. Also declined as axes: pendulum_height and arm_length, which are scale, and the sweep's union-AABB camera divides scale straight back out. And soft_body_pressure, the dead export: the pad is a stretched membrane, not a closed volume, so a pressure coefficient would have nothing to act on - wiring it would be a second promotion wearing this one's clothes.
dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED THE ARTIFACT IS NOT MERELY UNSETTLED, IT IS UNREPEATABLE IN PRINCIPLE. Zero linear_damp and zero angular_damp on both RigidBody3Ds means the pendulum never rests; the opening impulse arrives on a deferred idle call whose offset from the physics tick varies; and a double pendulum amplifies that difference exponentially. At the sweep's 1.1 s settle (plus the 0.35 s pre-pass) the arm is somewhere in its second swing and where is a coin toss. initial_impulse 0.0 means the deferred kick is never scheduled. settle_damp 6.0 sets linear_damp and angular_damp with DAMP_MODE_REPLACE on both bodies. lean_force 26.0 sets RigidBody3D.constant_force to (0, 0, -26) on the lower arm, so instead of striking once the arm swings once and comes to REST pressing on the anvil: a heavily damped system under a constant force has an ATTRACTING FIXED POINT, and two runs that both arrive near it produce the same picture regardless of how many ticks they took to get there. (The approved design said apply_central_force every _physics_process; constant_force is the engine's own version of that force, applied inside the physics step rather than once per rendered frame, which is strictly more repeatable on a bench whose frame rate is not fixed. _physics_process stays the no-op it already was.) SETTLING, RECOMPUTED - AND THE CORRECTION CHANGED THE CODE. A damp figure of 6.0 is a rate on VELOCITY, not a settling time constant, and here the two differ by 6.5x. The rig is overdamped (I 51.75 kg m2, k 242.4 N m/rad, wn 2.164 rad/s, zeta 1.386), so it settles on its SLOW pole at -0.922 /s, tau 1.08 s. From plumb the paddle first TOUCHES the anvil at t = 1.319 s, and capture_config_sweep shoots the render instance after ONE settle of 1.1 s - its 0.35 s pre-pass is a separate probe that is freed again (line 285), so the two do not add. The paddle was therefore 5.8 cm SHORT of the anvil in every tile: four photographs of the same untouched arm with different scenery behind it, which would have scored a confident bite made entirely of furniture. Neither fixture knob rescues it - raising lean_force scales the anvil's angle WITH the force so the time to first contact is invariant, and raising settle_damp makes it WORSE, the slow pole going as k/(I d). So _pose_lean() BUILDS each value at its own rest state instead of waiting for one: at anvil=none both links are placed at their true free equilibrium (13.56 and 14.86 degrees - NOT equal, the upper link carrying the lower one's weight as well as its own), and at slab/cushion/curtain both are placed at _anvil_lean(), which puts the paddle's front face exactly on the anvil plane at frame 0 with the lean still pressing it there. Each link is rotated about ITS OWN joint, so both PinJoint3D anchors stay coincident to machine precision - verified algebraically, joint1 error 0.0 and joint2 error 2.8e-17 - and nothing snaps when the simulation starts. What is left to settle is the contact itself and the small internal rearrangement between the two links, both governed by the FAST pole at 5.08 /s (tau 0.20 s), gone inside 0.6 s of the budget. pendulum_height 3.4 / arm_length 1.5 / paddle_size 0.7 shrink the rig so the anvil is a readable share of the frame; every anvil dimension is written in units of arm_length and paddle_size, so the scale change costs nothing. No RNG anywhere in the script - zero randf/randi calls - so there is no seed to set.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: cushion vs curtain, written before the capture. Both are compliant, both are SoftBody3D surfaces on the same contact plane, both wear the same off-white, and the hottest 5% falls inside the anvil region. The anvil occupies about 0.97 m of a 3.4 m fixtured rig, roughly 28% of frame height and 50% of width at framing 0.70 = about 14% of frame area; roughly 55% of that region's silhouette differs between the two (the arm, the posts and the head bars are common), so frame about 7.7% and focus about 30%. If cushion and curtain come back under 2% the membrane is too stiff to dent at lean_force 26 - lower ANVIL_LEAN_FRACTION so more of the travel is blocked, and do NOT reach for lean_force: _anvil_lean() scales the anvil's angle WITH the force, so raising it moves the target out by exactly as much as it pushes harder and the contact geometry does not change at all. (That sentence used to say 'raise the lean'. It was wrong, and it would have cost a pass.) RESIDUAL MOTION, named here so it is not met later as a surprise: _pose_lean() leaves none dead still at its true equilibrium, and slab and cushion in contact that resists, but CURTAIN is the one value still creeping at the shutter - a slack sheet barely resists, so the arm continues from the 8.92 degree contact angle toward its 14.86 degree free rest and is about 56% of the way there at 1.1 s, moving 1.8 mm per physics tick at the paddle. That is roughly one pixel per tick at this framing, and it is deterministic (no RNG, no chaos in an overdamped creep), so the honest claim is repeatable-to-about-a-pixel rather than bit-identical. It is also why the none-vs-curtain pair below may separate MORE than predicted rather than less. SECOND PREDICTION, worth more because it disagrees with the first: the pair most likely to collapse is none vs curtain measured on the ARM ALONE - a slack sheet gives almost no resistance, so the arm rests within a degree or two of where it rests with nothing there, and the entire difference between those two tiles is the presence of the sheet rather than any change in the pose.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config builds a signature of all seven values the build reads - anvil, pendulum_height, arm_length, paddle_size, initial_impulse, settle_damp, lean_force - and returns before touching anything when it matches the signature _ready() recorded. An unknown anvil word is dropped by the ANVILS allow-list before the signature is taken, so a typo keeps the shipped void rather than publishing a silent variant. A real change tears down only the nodes in _owned (detached before queue_free, so a replacement cannot collide with a freed node's name) and rebuilds synchronously in one call. _exit_tree() frees only _owned too, replacing a loop that freed EVERY child without an owner - which included anything the grid attached to the artifact after spawn.

dna.was: DERIVED, not composed. The axis, its allow-list, the five builders and the guarded apply_grid_config were already in commons/artifacts/jelly_cube/jelly_cube.gd (committed d3b41fbab) and the registry had never been told, so check_dna_declarations listed jelly_cube under 'promoted in code, undeclared in the registry' and the sweep could not reach any of it. What this pass added is the declaration and nothing else - not one line of the artifact was touched, because the code was already right: apply_grid_config returns unless the word is in the allow-list AND differs from the word already standing AND is_node_ready(), and _read_dna_meta lets a token's word be built once in _ready instead of built and torn down a frame later.
dna.note: assay is the softbody bench family's word and its five values, character for character - grab_jelly_bench, mass_spring_bench, energy_landscape_bench, membrane_bench, rigidity_dial_bench, abject_bench, octopus_bench, becoming_bench and tentacle_grab_bench all ask what apparatus a specimen is surrounded by, and jelly_cube stands in the same softbodies sequence as every one of them. The kit is re-dimensioned by a single factor u = cube_size / 0.5 so the family's proportions, accents and captions survive at this artifact's smaller scale; `control` is the rung that argues hardest, because an empty wire cage at the size the cube had BEFORE anything happened to it turns a thing you are watching into a difference you could disagree with.
dna.still_note: THE JIGGLE IS NOT AN AXIS AND CANNOT BE, and this is why the apparatus carries the claim instead. Everything jelly_cube exposes - stiffness, damping, pressure, mass - is a STARTING CONDITION on a body that relaxes, so five cubes started five ways settle into the same shape and photograph as one object five times; cloth_straps hit exactly this and took `suspension` for the same reason. Every assay rung is standing geometry: a graduated column, a wire reference cage, a plotted board, a glass case. The chart's settling trace is CLOSED FORM (exp(-3.4f)cos(13f)) and not sampled from the running solver, because a plot that came out different every launch would be noise wearing the costume of a record.
dna.framing_note: unchecked against a capture in this pass. The subject is a 0.3 m cube on a 0.42 m plinth, and _create_vr_controls already hangs a rack panel at z = 0.36 tilted -30 degrees; `chart` adds a board behind at -0.31 and `control` a second plate 0.35 m to the right, so the union-of-variants camera is pulled well back from the jelly itself. The @identity truth says 'a mushroom cap does not decide its shape - the pin constraint, gravity and whatever bumps into it negotiate the form', and the tissue doing the negotiating was hard-coded at one setting. The four values will differ in the frame - turgid holds a ball while slack has already collapsed - but the picture is a snapshot of a negotiation in progress, not four rest states. dna.default: relaxation=worked, and the word returns the literal 4 that line 85 already declares (`@export var constraint_passes: int = 4`) and that `_make_sim` has always handed to the solver. It is a SHORT-CIRCUIT, not a formula that lands near it: RELAXATION_PASSES is a const dict with the integer 4 written out, so `sim.constraint_passes` is assigned the same value from the same table on every build. The pre-existing numeric contract survives intact — a config carrying `constraint_passes` sets `_passes_pinned` and `_effective_passes()` returns the number instead, so the word can never override a map written before this promotion. Both fixture exports are exact no-ops at their defaults: `still = false` selects the original gust branch character for character (`gust = sin(_t * 0.8) * 0.6`, `gravity = Vector3(gust, -3.0, 0.3 * sin(_t * 0.5))`, dial `sin(_t * 0.3) * 0.6`, sway `sin(_t * 0.25) * 0.06`), and `settle_steps = 60` is the literal count the shipped `for _i in 60` ran. ONE PLACEMENT in 2420 maps: FormFinding_Relaxation, token `verlet_workbench:90` — a rotation suffix and nothing else, so merged_config is empty, GridInteractablesComponent never calls apply_grid_config, and that placement never reaches a line this promotion added. No exhibit_furniture mount and no curation roster names it. The one behavioural change at the default is the deletion of `_rng.randomize()`; `_rng` is inherited from embodied_prop.gd and read nowhere in this file (grep: zero hits), so nothing observes it, and leaving it would have been a loaded gun for the next person who adds a randf to _build.
dna.was: a dial, a readout and a claim — none of them reachable by name. `constraint_passes` was already a clamped config key and `_readout_text` already printed `passes: %d`, so the bench could always be told to relax harder; but no map ever told it to, and there was no word a sweep could use. More seriously, it had no resting state at all: `_process` drove `_sim.gravity` from `sin(_t * 0.8)` off the wall clock and re-ran the integrator once per RENDERED frame, so the pose was a function of both elapsed time and frame count. Measured on a python replica of soft_body_sim.step(): with the gust running, `worked` moves 25.6 mm of max vertex displacement between render frame 66 and frame 90 — three times the entire worked-to-held separation of 8.5 mm. Any bite number taken from the shipped artifact would have been a fact about the shutter.
dna.note: `relaxation` is SHARED with cloth_simulation in this same wave, deliberately and character for character — apply_dna_block derived the same four values in the same order from two independent solvers: soft_body_sim's `for _p in constraint_passes` with a stiffness gain of 0.75, and ClothSimulation.gd's own iteration loop with a hard-coded gain. It is the same question, how insistently is a distance constraint enforced, so their bite numbers should ORDER the same way and sit within about a factor of two of each other; if they do not, that disagreement is evidence about the harness rather than about either design. The word exists at all because apply_dna_block refuses a numeric axis by design — sample points on a continuum are a design choice, not a fact about the code — so the four points are named here and derived there: nudged = 1, worked = 4 (the shipped literal), pressed = 8, held = 12. This artifact already WAS this axis; @identity states the claim outright (crank the passes up and the cloth stiffens; drop them and it sags — yet no linear system is ever solved). What was missing was the word.
dna.declined: `damping` (0.99), the purest rate axis in the sequence: four values reach the SAME drape, some sooner, and a still cannot tell them apart at rest — declined by name because this wave exists to refuse exactly that. The gust amplitudes (0.6 lateral, 0.3 in Z) move the cloth about seven times as far as the whole axis does and are still wrong, because they are a DRIVE: `sin(_t * 0.8)` never stops, so photographing them is photographing the clock, and the fixture's entire job is to switch them off. Cloth resolution (cloth_cols 10 / cloth_rows 8 / cell 0.085) is a real and interesting claim — the discretization IS the material — but `grain` is already the corpus's word for how a body is subdivided, across six artifacts with a different value set, and inventing a seventh synonym to serve ONE placement is worse than shipping one axis that is exactly right. The pin mode (`top_corners`, with six values already sitting in soft_body_shapes._cloth_is_pin) is flagdancer's `heading` in this same wave; if verlet_workbench ever wants it, the honest move is to take flagdancer's word and values, not a synonym.
dna.fixture_why: AS SHIPPED THIS ARTIFACT IS NEVER AT REST, so without this fixture every number the sweep produces is about the frame clock rather than about the material. `still` zeroes the four things the bench drives off the wall clock — the lateral gust, the Z gust, the bench sway and the dial spin — in one guarded branch, so `_sim.gravity` holds the constant (0, -3, 0) the pre-settle already used and both rotating nodes hold rotation 0. `settle_steps` raises the existing SYNCHRONOUS pre-settle from 60 to 420 so every value reaches ITS OWN fixed point before frame 1. All of this is measured on a python replica of soft_body_sim.step() rather than argued: at 420 steps the pose is 0.050 mm from the 2400-step pose for nudged and bit-identical for worked, pressed and held; 66 further rendered frames then move nudged by 0.066 mm and the other three by 0.0000 mm. At the shipped 60 the same comparison moves nudged by 21.0 mm — ten times the closest pair's separation — because at step 60 nudged is still in transient overshoot, moving 0.88 mm in step 61 against 0.0010 mm in step 421. The step SIZE cannot drift with frame rate: soft_body_sim.step takes `dt: float = 0.0166667` and no caller passes another. The simulator holds no RNG and `_rng.randomize()` is deleted, so with the pose fixed in _ready two runs of one value are the same picture.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config assigns every key it accepts, then compares `_build_signature()` — relaxation, the effective pass count, cloth_cols, cloth_rows, cell, emissive, stiffness, all four colours, still and settle_steps — and RETURNS before touching a live simulation when nothing the build reads has changed. Teardown walks an `_owned: Array[Node]` rather than `get_children()`, which is what the shipped version did: that loop freed every child on every config call, taking any plinth, highlight, collider or pickup plumbing the grid had attached down with the artifact, and it rebuilt unconditionally because there was no signature to compare. _ready() builds synchronously and there is no call_deferred anywhere in the build path.
dna.predicted_degeneracy: pressed vs held, and the arithmetic is the solver's own fixed-point law. Residual stretch scales as 1/(passes x gain) at gain 0.75, so the four values sit at 1.33 / 0.33 / 0.167 / 0.111 residual units and the last two are 0.056 apart against nudged-to-worked's 1.0 — 18:1 predicted. MEASURED on the replica at settle 420, as max vertex displacement: pressed-vs-held 2.154 mm and nudged-vs-worked 34.458 mm, a ratio of 16.0:1. The law holds and the prediction was 12% high. NOW THE PART THAT CAN BE WRONG, and it is about pixels rather than millimetres. The camera does not move between tiles: the merged MeshInstance3D AABB is 1.32 x 1.34 x 0.70 for all four values, because the cloth hangs between y 0.659 and 1.30 and never touches a face of it. At dna.framing 0.65 the frame is 2.479 m over 760 px, i.e. 3.261 mm/px — which puts pressed-vs-held at 0.66 px, SUB-PIXEL, and nudged-vs-worked at 10.6 px across a cloth holding 7.6% of frame. And the cloth is flat-shaded: _rebuild_cloth_mesh writes Vector3.UP into every normal, so its interior is a near-uniform emissive field and almost all of the change is SILHOUETTE, not shading. Counting the moving edge (a 235 px bottom travelling ~10.6 px, plus two 186 px sides averaging half of that) gives roughly 4,500 changed pixels out of 577,600. PREDICT nudged-vs-worked frame ~0.8%, focus ~9%; pressed-vs-held frame ~0.05%, focus ~1%. THE RISK IS NAMED HERE RATHER THAN DISCOVERED LATER: the frame number will look weak and only focus can carry this axis over the bar. If the whole axis reads under 2% on focus, suspect the harness before the ladder — check that `settle_steps` arrived as the integer 420 and not the string, and that `still` arrived as a bool — because the ladder is four genuinely different equilibria and is not in doubt. If it is real but faint, the remedy is dna.framing 0.45, which doubles the cloth to 15.8% of frame at the cost of cropping the readout panel.
dna.framing_why: The merged MeshInstance3D AABB is 1.32 x 1.34 x 0.70, radius 1.0035, and it is the SAME box for every value of the axis — the cloth sits comfortably inside it on all three axes, so the camera is genuinely fixed across the tiles rather than approximately so. At framing 1.0 the visible half-extent is radius x PAD = 1.0035 x 1.9 = 1.907 m and the 0.765 x 0.607 m cloth is only 3.2% of frame, under the ~6% floor. 0.65 brings the half-extent to 1.239 m and the cloth to 7.6%. It is chosen over the tighter 0.45 because 1.239 m still exceeds the AABB's circumscribed radius of 1.0035 m, so NOTHING is cropped: the constraint-pass dial and the `passes: N` readout stay in frame, and they are half of this artifact's argument — the readout says in digits what the cloth says in its silhouette.

dna.default: platen=plate, give=jelly. `plate` makes _under_platen() return true unconditionally, so the clamp loop runs character for character as shipped: `if _sim.positions[i].y > ceil_y: _sim.positions[i].y = ceil_y` over every particle, and _make_platen() falls through to the literal _box(Vector3(0, 0.08 + _block_top0 + 0.05, 0), Vector3(block_size + 0.18, 0.05, block_size + 0.18), _steel_mat(plate_col)). `jelly` is a SHORT-CIRCUIT, not a copy: it is absent from GIVE_STIFFNESS and _stiffness() returns the `stiffness` export itself, so 0.85 stays a single literal and a map that sets stiffness by hand still works. The three fixture exports are no-ops at their defaults: held_phase -1.0 fails the `>= 0.0` guard so the whole held branch is skipped and _press_amount() computes the shipped fmod; settle_steps 30 is the shipped loop count; block_cells 3 gives cell = block_size / 2.0, which is not an approximation of `block_size * 0.5` but the same IEEE-754 value, division and multiplication by a power of two both being exact. _block_top(true) masks to the platen only when platen != plate, so at the default it is the shipped unmasked loop. The one behavioural change at the default is _rng.randomize() becoming _rng.seed = 20260812, and `_rng` is inherited from embodied_prop.gd and read nowhere in this file, so nothing observes it. ONE PLACEMENT: Grown_Applied_Softbody, token `elasticity_press:180:0.0` — a rotation and an explicit y_offset with no #key:value tail, so merged_config is empty, GridInteractablesComponent never calls apply_grid_config, and the placement never reaches the new code at all. No exhibit_furniture mount and no curation roster names it. ADJACENT FINDING, not fixed in this pass and recorded so it is not lost: that explicit `:0.0` third field is the name:rot:0.0 form that suppresses auto-grounding, so this artifact may be standing at raw y=0 rather than seated on the floor at its measured base.
dna.was: one press and one claim about pressing: a flat ceiling over EVERY particle, which is an infinitely wide platen and a decision about the tool that nobody had argued. And no resting state at all — the pose was fmod(_t, press_period) off the wall clock, so the block was never anywhere in particular. Worse, and only visible once the simulation was actually run: the 30-step pre-settle is nowhere near long enough for the block to fall the 0.75 m make_jelly_grid starts it above the floor, so the shipped artifact photographs a block still in MID-AIR, hanging 0.63 m clear of the press base and intersecting the top beam, with _block_top0 = 1.1312. That figure is measured, on a Python port of soft_body_sim and again analytically — during free fall the springs are at rest length and do nothing, so the top layer's drop is just the damped Verlet series from 1.25, which sums to 0.1188 m in 30 steps. (An earlier draft of this entry estimated 1.105 by hand and was wrong by 26 mm; the number here is the one the solver produces.) A fully settled block tops out at 0.4988. settle_steps 260 lands it on the base where it belongs.
dna.note: `platen` is NEW and free corpus-wide. Not `press` (unused but vague), not `mould` — a mould implies form imposed from outside and this sequence's line is that form is NOT imposed; the platen constrains and the springs decide. Not `apparatus` or `assay`: those name what SURROUNDS a specimen, and four artifacts in this sequence already carry `assay`; the platen is in contact with the specimen and is doing the work. `give` is NEW as a word and chosen against three near neighbours on purpose. NOT `flesh` (soft_mushroom: soft/turgid/slack/firm is tissue quality at rest in a growing body, and it moves SoftBody3D stiffness, damping AND pressure together). NOT `substance` (breathing_room: solid/flesh/glass/fabric is what a slab is MADE of, an appearance axis). NOT `temper` (spring_hopper: spring gauge in a hopper mechanism). `give` is one mechanical property under a named load, and its values name a material only as a way of saying how much it yields. The two axes are the two halves of one negotiation: platen is the tool's half, give is the material's.
dna.declined: `press_period` (4.0), the cycle rate — the single most tempting export in the file because it is the one thing the artifact obviously DOES. Refused: at the fixed shutter a 2 s period and an 8 s period put the plate at completely different heights, so a sweep of it returns four confidently different pictures and a strong bite number that is entirely a fact about the frame clock and not about the material. That is the exact failure this wave exists to refuse, and it would have passed every gate. Also declined: `damping` (0.9 — pure decay, invisible once the thing is at rest) and `travel` (block_size x 0.45 — how far the plate goes, a scale on one axis that the union-AABB camera partly divides back out, and anyway the same claim as `give` seen from the tool's side).
dna.fixture_why:
AS SHIPPED THIS ARTIFACT IS NEVER AT REST, so without this fixture every number the sweep produces is about the frame clock. held_phase 0.5 replaces fmod(_t, press_period)/press_period with a constant everywhere the cycle is read: at phase exactly 0.5 the code's `if phase < 0.5` is false, giving 1.0 - 0.0/0.5 = 1.0, then smoothstep(1.0) = 1.0 — maximum compression, where both axes argue loudest. The plate is then HELD and _t selects nothing. settle_steps 260 runs TWO passes: an unloaded settle that lands the block on the base and fixes _block_top0, then a second 260 steps under the SAME masked ceiling the frame loop applies, so frame 0 is the loaded pose rather than the squeeze happening. 260 is chosen with margin on the first pass and measured: the unloaded top converges to 0.4969 m by step ~180 and is unchanged at 400 and at 1200. block_cells 5 is a bench knob, not a cheat: cell = block_size/(block_cells-1) holds the block's extent at exactly 0.5 m, and at the shipped 3 it is a byte-identical no-op. It matters because at 27 particles the sphere radius is block_size x 0.16 = 0.08 against a spacing of 0.25, so the block photographs as a loose dot cloud and a punch mark one particle wide is not a picture of anything; at 125 the spacing is 0.125 against a 0.16 diameter, the spheres overlap, and the block reads as a solid whose surface can take a mark. 

`frozen` IS THE ONE THAT MAKES THE MEASUREMENT REAL, and it is here because the arithmetic said the other three were not enough. A HELD PLATE DOES NOT IMPLY A STILL BLOCK. soft_body_sim was ported to Python and the loaded pose measured directly: at platen = punch the worst particle still travels 9.8e-2 m per 87-frame shutter window, and it is 9.8e-2 m after 5,000 loaded steps exactly as it is after 260. ring holds at ~1.1e-2 m and wedge at ~5e-3 m. Only plate is genuinely still, at 1.3e-5 m. This is a LIMIT CYCLE the clamp itself drives, not a transient waiting to decay, so no settle count reaches it: _press_ceiling moves a particle's position without touching prev_position — unlike the sim's own floor collision, which sets both — so every step it fires it injects velocity, and under a narrow tool the surrounding material drags the clamped column back above the ceiling every step, so it fires forever. (Mirroring the floor's prev-clamp was tried and REJECTED by measurement: it converges nothing and destabilises plate, from 1.3e-5 to 8.6e-3.) That would still be survivable if the shutter counted frames. It does not — capture_config_sweep waits `await create_timer(SETTLE).timeout`, a wall-clock 1.1 s, while _process steps the sim once per rendered frame — so the step count at the shutter is a fact about the achieved frame rate, and on a limit cycle two runs of one value are two different pictures. That is precisely the failure press_period was declined for, arriving by the back door and through a knob nobody would have suspected. Frozen, _process returns before touching anything and the pose is a pure function of (platen, give, block_size, block_cells, settle_steps): no clock, no delta, no frame count. Cost: 520 pre-settle steps on a 125-particle, 540-spring lattice, roughly 1.8M inner operations in _ready(), and then zero per-frame work forever. Nothing shipped pays any of it — the default is 30 steps on 27 particles with _process running exactly as it always did.
dna.rebuild_guard: apply_grid_config assigns every key it accepts, then compares _signature() — platen, give, block_size, stiffness, held_phase, settle_steps, block_cells, emissive, block_col — and RETURNS before touching a live simulation when nothing the build reads has changed. press_period is deliberately excluded: nothing in _build() reads it, so a period-only change takes effect on the next frame without restarting the material. Teardown frees an _owned array rather than walking get_children(), which the shipped version did — that took any plinth, highlight or host-parented node down with the artifact. No call_deferred anywhere in the build path; _ready() builds synchronously.
dna.predicted_degeneracy:
PREDICTED, before any capture. platen: PUNCH vs WEDGE, because both are small tools that leave most of the top face untouched and both dent the centre. Discrete arithmetic, since block_cells 5 puts the columns at x,z in {-0.25,-0.125,0,0.125,0.25}: punch (radius <= 0.11) catches 1 column of 25, wedge (|z| <= 0.05) catches the 5 at z=0, ring (radius >= 0.15) catches 20 — so punch and wedge differ over 4 columns, 16% of the top face. The top face is ~15% of the silhouette and the subject ~50% of frame at framing 0.45, giving ~1.2% of frame from the material plus ~1% from the tool meshes. PREDICT frame ~2.2%, focus ~12%. give: JELLY vs RUBBER, 0.85 against 0.93, predicted frame ~0.8% and focus ~3.5% — at or under the bite bar, named as a risk rather than discovered as a disappointment.

THEN THE POSE WAS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED, on a Python port of soft_body_sim run at the exact fixture (block_cells 5, 260 unloaded + 260 loaded steps, held at full squeeze), and it disagrees with both predictions. This is written down BEFORE the capture so the critic's numbers can be compared against something that was not tuned to them.

platen — the axis is far stronger than predicted, and the closest pair is probably the WRONG ONE. Frozen block geometry, give=jelly: plate top 0.2491 / width 0.5079 / height 0.2501; punch 0.4949 / 0.7060 / 0.5134; wedge 0.4914 / 0.5900 / 0.5059; ring 0.2559 / 0.5427 / 0.2621. Block height spans 2.05x and width 1.39x across the four — these are four different solids, not four dents. Punch and wedge do agree closely on TOP (0.4949 vs 0.4914, 3.5 mm) as predicted, but they differ by 116 mm in width, 20% of the block. The genuinely close pair on the material is PLATE vs RING — tops 0.2491 vs 0.2559, widths 0.5079 vs 0.5427 — which the prediction did not consider at all. Both pairs are then separated by their tool meshes (a 0.68 m slab against an annulus with a 0.30 m hole; a 0.22 m disc against a 0.68 x 0.10 m blade), so the expected degeneracy is low in both cases; if a pair does come back flat, look at plate/ring first.

give — EXPECT THIS TO FAIL, and the named fallback will not rescue it. At the frozen pose under platen=plate the four values give block widths of 0.5081 (gel) / 0.5079 (jelly) / 0.5047 (rubber) / 0.5025 (resin), and mid-height waists within 5 mm of each other. The whole axis spans 5.6 mm, about 1.1% of the block's width, on a block that is ~11% of frame — comfortably under any bite bar. The prediction's physical story is also backwards: it expected the stiffer values to spread WIDER, and the stiffest is in fact the narrowest. The mechanism is that `stiffness` in this solver is not a modulus, it is the relaxation rate of the distance-constraint pass (correction = (cur - rest) * 0.5 * stiffness). It sets how FAST the material reaches its fixed point, and the fixed point itself is set by the rest lengths, the floor and the platen ceiling — which are identical for all four values. The only residual dependence is the sag needed to balance gravity, and gravity here is 2.0 m/s^2 over a 1/60 step, so that term is ~1e-3 of the clamp displacement. Note the bind this puts the fixture in: stiffness was visible only as a difference in how far along the transient the block had got, and `frozen` — which the platen axis needs in order to be reproducible at all — is exactly what removes that regime. The two halves of the negotiation are not symmetric after all. Moving rubber to 0.70, the fallback the design named, cannot help: gel at 0.45 is already near the clamp's floor of 0.40 and the entire legal range spans those same 5.6 mm. If this axis is to argue anything it needs to move something that changes the EQUILIBRIUM — the spring topology, say, a gel without the face diagonals against a resin with them — which is a different axis and a separate pass, not a tuning of this one.
dna.framing_why: The union AABB is the press frame, 1.14 x 1.12 x 0.70 — the block is a MultiMeshInstance3D and contributes nothing to it, which is a gift here: the box is identical for all eight tiles, so the camera truly does not move. But radius x PAD = 0.872 x 1.9 = 1.66 m of visible half-extent at framing 1.0 puts a 0.5 m block at 2.3% of frame area, well under the ~6% floor. At 0.45 the half-extent is 0.746 m and the block is ~11%. The worst subject corner that must survive is the platen's far-left-back at a screen offset of ~0.57 m, which leaves ~30% margin; the billboard truth line at y=1.5 falls outside and the top beam is cropped, which is the intended trade.
